prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports (keep safety authority): Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Elements: Demand Prediction Service (DPS, Marlinstone; unconstrained demand); Capacity Assessment Module (AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate); Slot Allocation Engine (SAE, Blueharbor; CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time); Departure Metering Service (DMS, Emberline; optional Passenger Misconnect Count); these reject data lacking Time Synchronization Service timestamp. Airport CDM Portal; Identity Access Service (IAS); Audit Event Ledger; Alert Distribution Hub (Digital Briefing Room); Performance Analytics Warehouse; Collaborative Decision Log; Business Rules Registry; Tower Sequence Manager; Ramp Movement Board; North/South Runway Meter; East/West Apron Sensor; Gate Conflict Detector; Surface Surveillance Adapter; Weather Ingest Gateway; Flight Data Exchange (Flight Intent Message, realized times); Airline Interface Adapter; Handling Resource Planner; Sector Load Monitor; Common Situation Display; Contingency Operations Console; Arrival Regulation Console; Post Operations Report; Airport Capacity Plan. Silverpine: emergency access only after IAS records incident reference/expiry. Actors: Airline Operations Coordinator (TOBT=Target Off Block Time); Aircraft Operator Representative (Flight Intent Messages; Decision Log challenges); Regional Flow Manager (RFM); Slot Coordinator; Data Governance Steward (DGS); Meteorology Briefing Officer; Airport Duty Manager (ADM; Capacity Plan, mode changes); Tower Supervisor; System Support Engineer (SSE); Ramp Control Lead; Ground Handling Dispatcher; Network Operations Liaison; Airspace Sector Planner; Emergency Response Coordinator; Deicing Coordinator. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather; Capacity Reduction; Recovery; Slot Compliance; Contingency Fallback (ADM declares after consulting RFM; RFM may direct if Platform unsafe). No silent mode changes. Deployment: Readiness Gates 2-4, waves, RFM declares full deployment. SSE: 24/7 on-call, advises only; keeps incident records referencing Audit Event Ledger; verifies fallback tools/exports/restoration checkpoints before advising resumption. Decision Log preserves major-incident context. Post-incident review for critical, repeated high-priority, security, constrained-ops failures; corrective actions to named owners. Changes: night windows coordinated with RFM, ADM, Tower Supervisor, AOR groups; Rules Registry/IAS/Time Sync/Flight Data Exchange/metering changes need test-environment validation;

New part:
S937: The first expansion path is the exchange of cross-border flow constraints, demand forecasts, and agreed measures with adjacent regional systems under defined governance arrangements.
S938: This capability would allow the Regional Flow Manager and Network Operations Liaison to see upstream demand pressure earlier and to negotiate measures before local capacity is saturated.
S939: Cross-border exchange should use standardized message structures where practical, but the Business Rules Registry should retain the local parameters needed for Meridian operations.
S940: The Flight Data Exchange should be enhanced to accept richer intent data, including improved route options, expected cruise profiles, and updated departure readiness information.
S941: The Demand Prediction Service should use this data to create more stable demand pictures across longer planning horizons while still preserving tactical responsiveness.
S942: Trajectory prediction should also make greater use of weather features, sector configuration, runway direction, and surface movement status when estimating flight progress.
S943: The Weather Ingest Gateway and Sector Load Monitor should provide the common inputs needed to connect airspace capacity and airport capacity in the same prediction cycle.
S944: The Capacity Assessment Module should evolve from a mainly rules-based assessment into a service that can compare planned capacity, observed throughput, and predicted constraint persistence.
S945: Any use of learning models should be introduced with explainability requirements so that operational users can understand why a capacity or delay estimate has changed.
S946: Advanced turnaround prediction should combine aircraft state, handling milestones, stand occupancy, crew readiness, passenger processing, and ramp congestion signals.
S947: The Airport CDM Portal, Airline Interface Adapter, Handling Resource Planner, and Ramp Movement Board should provide the main operational inputs for this capability.
S948: Predicted changes to Target Off Block Time should be presented with confidence levels rather than as unconditional system corrections.
S949: The Slot Allocation Engine should use improved turnaround predictions to protect feasible Calculated Takeoff Time assignments and to reduce avoidable re-sequencing.
S950: The Tower Sequence Manager and Departure Metering Service should receive only the information needed for tactical sequencing, with detailed airline operational data controlled by policy.
S951: Machine-assisted recovery options should support the Recovery Phase by proposing coordinated actions that balance runway throughput, sector loading, stand availability, and airline priorities.
S952: These options should be generated by the Contingency Operations Console and reviewed through the Common Situation Display before any operational decision is applied.
S953: The system should not automatically impose a Ground Delay Program, change an Airport Acceptance Rate, or alter a tactical measure without authorized human confirmation.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
